mon-001.voice: Someone rich will send you money. Just wait for it.
mon-001.situation: Daydreaming that a wealthy relative or patron will bail you out.

mon-002.voice: When real poverty hits, no one will help you.
mon-002.situation: Fear of being poor and alone, with no one to turn to.

excerpt.to: the LORD will be my God,

mon-003.voice: Your parents gave you nothing. They deserve your contempt.
mon-003.situation: Resentment toward parents over money or an inheritance.

mon-004.voice: Put the new person to work. Make them earn their place.
mon-004.situation: Loading a newcomer with burdens for your own gain.

mon-005.voice: Keep it for yourself. Their need isn’t your problem.
mon-005.situation: Withholding compassion from someone who asks for help.

mon-006.voice: Keep them busy earning. Study and prayer can wait.
mon-006.situation: Pushing others toward profit at the cost of their spiritual growth.

mon-007.voice: They’ve been sick for so long. They’re a drain.
mon-007.situation: Neglecting someone who is chronically ill and poor.

mon-008.voice: They can work harder than that. Push them.
mon-008.situation: Demanding more of someone than they can give.

mon-009.voice: Say no. You can’t afford to lend.
mon-009.situation: Refusing a loan to someone in real need.

mon-010.voice: Store it up. Don’t let anyone else dip into it.
mon-010.situation: Keeping your resources locked away from others.

mon-011.voice: Grow your wealth. Who wants a simple life?
mon-011.situation: Choosing to build wealth over a life of simplicity.
mon-011.note: Gideon’s answer: a little, gleaned humbly, can be better than the whole harvest.

mon-012.voice: Why did I give that money away? That was a mistake.
mon-012.situation: Regretting your generosity right after giving.

mon-013.voice: I can follow Jesus and keep a safety net.
mon-013.situation: Wanting to follow Christ fully while holding on to some wealth.
mon-013.note: When Elisha left everything to follow Elijah, he slaughtered his oxen, cooked them over his plowing gear and fed the people.

mon-014.voice: Guests again? I can’t keep spending on them.
mon-014.situation: Being stingy with what you have when people come to you.

mon-015.voice: This money was given for others, but I could use some of it.
mon-015.situation: Tempted to spend money entrusted to you on yourself.

excerpt.from: Is it a time to receive money

mon-015.note: Gehazi took silver and clothing from Naaman behind Elisha’s back. Evagrius sees love of money as the first link in a long chain of sins.

mon-016.voice: You gave up your inheritance. Look what you’ve lost.
mon-016.situation: Grieving the money or inheritance you gave up for God.

mon-017.voice: Your family has abandoned you. They won’t help.
mon-017.situation: Feeling abandoned by family when money is tight.

mon-018.voice: Your siblings are rich and admired. Look at you.
mon-018.situation: Envy of relatives or peers who are wealthy and respected.

mon-019.voice: My money is mine to use however I like.
mon-019.situation: Forgetting you will answer for how you use what God has given.

mon-020.voice: I want my parents’ house and property.
mon-020.situation: Clinging to family property and the life of this world.

mon-021.voice: Think about getting rich. Imagine it.
mon-021.situation: Daydreaming about wealth without seeing what it costs you.

mon-022.voice: Your parents’ home was so much nicer than this.
mon-022.situation: Comparing your modest place with the comfort you left behind.

mon-023.voice: You need money for the things you have to have.
mon-023.situation: Relying on money instead of God’s grace for your needs.

mon-024.voice: I keep thinking about money: what I had, could get, must protect.
mon-024.situation: Persistent thoughts about money, past, future and present.

mon-025.voice: Be generous to them now. You can use them later.
mon-025.situation: Using hospitality as a hook for gain or influence.

mon-026.voice: You’ll be poor for years and years.

mon-027.voice: I’ll give something. Just barely enough.
mon-027.situation: Giving as little mercy as you can get away with.

mon-028.voice: You’re poor and unwell yourself. Help them tomorrow.
mon-028.situation: Putting off doing good with excuses of poverty or weakness.

mon-029.voice: Work day and night. Scripture and the sick can wait.
mon-029.situation: Working for money so much that prayer and caring for others drop away.

mon-030.situation: Anxiety that you’ve been too generous with your money.

mon-031.voice: Money is worth more than wisdom. Hold on to it.
mon-031.situation: Choosing money over the wisdom of compassion.

mon-032.voice: Get rich, and people will finally respect you.
mon-032.situation: Seeking comfort and status through wealth.

mon-033.voice: I gave, but I resent it.
mon-033.situation: Generosity spoiled by grumbling and regret.
mon-033.note: This line appears only in the Greek version of Proverbs.

mon-034.voice: Remember your old home, your things, your old life?
mon-034.situation: Memories of home and possessions pulling at your heart.

mon-035.voice: Keep what you have and get more. It’s for good causes.
mon-035.situation: Accumulating under pious pretexts like hospitality or buying books.

mon-036.situation: Picturing the loss of your money or property.

mon-037.voice: Stock up. Don’t hand it out to people who need it.
mon-037.situation: Stockpiling food and clothing instead of sharing.

mon-038.voice: I see their need, but I don’t feel moved.
mon-038.situation: Unmoved by the poverty of people around you.

mon-039.voice: They took what’s mine. I’ll sue.
mon-039.situation: Wanting to fight in court over what was taken from you.
mon-039.note: Evagrius warns that the mind stays chained to what was taken until, in love, it lets go of the cloak too.

mon-040.voice: Don’t lend it. They’ll never pay you back.
mon-040.situation: Refusing to lend because the person might not repay.

mon-041.voice: Build up your savings. Then you’ll be secure.
mon-041.situation: Wanting to amass wealth, and the anxiety that comes with it.

mon-042.voice: Get rich. You can serve God with the money.
mon-042.situation: Telling yourself wealth will make you a better servant of God.

mon-043.voice: I want others to help me, but I won’t help them.
mon-043.situation: Expecting help in hard times while ignoring other people’s needs.

mon-044.voice: Not this time. Keep your money.
mon-044.situation: Holding back when a good opportunity to share comes along.

mon-045.voice: I did the good thing, but I resent everyone involved.
mon-045.situation: Doing good while caught up in grudges, complaints and sour looks.

mon-046.voice: Your relatives have it made. They’re the lucky ones.
mon-046.situation: Envying others for their visible wealth.

mon-047.voice: Give less. Keep a little back.
mon-047.situation: Being sparing when you give to the poor.
mon-047.note: Evagrius observes that giving frees the mind, while regretting a gift binds it.

mon-048.situation: Money souring your kindness toward others.

mon-049.voice: Look out for yourself. Nobody else will.
mon-049.situation: Storing up possessions for yourself alone.

mon-050.voice: Think how much good you could do with the money you used to have.
mon-050.situation: Missing past wealth by imagining the good it could do.

mon-051.voice: A little greed is normal. It’s not like it’s idolatry.
mon-051.situation: Making peace with greed and not seeing it as idolatry.

mon-052.voice: Get a bit more than you need. Just in case.
mon-052.situation: Collecting more than you need, and wanting wealth.

mon-053.voice: Food and clothing aren’t enough. I need more.
mon-053.situation: Wanting more than the basics, forgetting you leave with nothing.

mon-054.voice: There’s nothing wrong with loving money. Think of the good it does.
mon-054.situation: Defending the love of money as harmless or even helpful.

mon-055.voice: Get into business. The profit will cover your needs.
mon-055.situation: Getting tangled in worldly affairs for the sake of profit.

mon-056.voice: The money’s gone and it won’t come back. Scramble!
mon-056.situation: Anxious busyness after money runs out.

mon-057.voice: They’re not really in need. Don’t give.
mon-057.situation: Dismissing someone’s need so you don’t have to give.

mon-058.voice: Say you love them. You don’t have to pay for it.
mon-058.situation: Loving others in words while money keeps you from loving in deeds.
